About

Split the Lark is a baroque ensemble led by singers. In our performances of repertoire from 1600-1800, we believe the vocal line clearly declaimed by a skilled soloist contains the necessary musical information to lead an ensemble.

Each Split the Lark score is prepared with text and translation at the beginning of the document. The vocal line is rendered as a small staff above each players’ part, allowing each player to shape their phrase along with the singers’ declamation of the text. The inclusion of the vocal line also eliminates guesswork around instrumental exits and entrances. After meeting at the Cesti Baroque Competition in Innsbruck, Austria, American singers Morgan Mastrangelo and Sarah Fleiss were troubled by the rarity of singers in positions of leadership within baroque music, particularly within ensembles that purport to specialize in baroque opera. Indeed, out of 80 member organizations within Early Music America, roughly 6% were led by singers.

The institutional dearth of singers in leadership positions has, we believe, accompanied a persistent unfamiliarity with the methods and principles necessary for successful operatic singing in the baroque style. Split the Lark was founded to uplift and model these principles on the highest possible level.

Italian Opera in the Age of the American Revolution

October 19, 2026 · The Italian Academy at Columbia University

Split the Lark's inaugural program recreates a slice of New York City's musical life circa 1776. Lesser-known arias by Thomas Arne and Niccolò Piccinni, premiered on American soil in Revolutionary-era New York, were Americans' first introductions to European concert music and shaped the aesthetics of the first generation of homegrown American musicians.

Arias from Handel, Vivaldi, and A. Scarlatti round out the program, contextualizing the Italianate operatic tradition that took root across the Atlantic.

"These two artists made every word count. We delighted in the generosity of dramatic interpretation and clarity of diction."Voce di Meche
  • Dormi, o fulmine di guerra Scarlatti
  • Gelido in ogni vena Vivaldi
  • Stragi, morti, sangue ed armi Handel
  • The Soldier Tir'd of War's Alarms Arne
  • Thou Like the Glorious Sun Arne
  • O Sleep, Why Dost Thou Leave Me Handel
  • Furie di donna irata Piccinni
  • Al trionfo del nostro furore Handel · duet

The development, performance, and recording of this program was supported by generous grants from the Mass Cultural Council and the Curtis Institute of Music’s Dietrich Alumni Fund.

The Artists

Morgan Mastrangelo

Tenor · Co-Director

Tenor Morgan Mastrangelo has been hailed as “terrific” (The New York Times) and “a standout” (Parterre Box). A recent alum of Boston Lyric Opera’s Emerging Artist Program, Morgan covered leading roles with the company for three seasons before making their principal debut as Ruodi in BLO’s new production of Guillaume Tell in September 2026.

Morgan’s 2025–26 season brought major role debuts in the US and Europe. At the Opéra Royal de Versailles, they sang Astolfe in Lully’s Roland with the period-instrument orchestra Ensemble I Gemelli, in a performance hailed as “incontestablement la révélation de cette soirée” (BaroquiadeS). They also sang Madeline X in Michael Gordon’s What to Wear at the PROTOTYPE Festival and Hades in Matthew Aucoin’s Eurydice with Opera Grand Rapids. This past summer, Morgan joined the Santa Fe Opera’s prestigious Apprentice Singers program, appearing as Don Ramiro in scenes from La Cenerentola. Their 2026–27 season brings a full role debut as Don Ramiro with the Boston Youth Symphony Orchestras and the tenor solos in Handel’s Messiah at Duke University Chapel.

Active on the concert stage, Morgan particularly adores Bach. With Bach Vespers New York, they recently sang the tenor solo in BWV 92 with conductor Harry Bicket and the solo cantata Ich armer Mensch, ich Sündenknecht, BWV 55. They made their Boston Baroque debut as the tenor soloist in the Coffee Cantata, BWV 211, and will sing the Evangelist in the St. Matthew Passion with the Amherst Bach Festival in 2027. With Emmanuel Music, they have sung the tenor solos in more than fifteen cantatas in the weekly Bach Cantata series.

Morgan is the co-founder and co-director of the period-instrument ensemble Split the Lark, whose inaugural New York concert — a program of rare Italian and English arias performed in Revolutionary-era America — sold out Columbia University’s Casa Italiana. They are a 2026 Sullivan Award winner, and took second prize at the Concours de Chant Baroque de Froville, the Handel Aria Competition, and the American National Oratorio Competition in 2025, following a second prize at the 2024 Lyndon-Woodside Oratorio Competition.

Sarah Fleiss

Soprano · Co-Director

Described as “bright and stylish” by Opera News and “sparkling” by Bachtrack, this season American soprano Sarah Fleiss is an Emerging Artist with Opera Philadelphia. She sings the title role in Handel’s Esther with Mountainside Baroque, and is the soprano soloist in Beethoven Mass in C with the Binghamton Symphony, Handel’s Messiah with the Wichita Symphony, Liszt’s Missa Solemnis with the Montgomery County Chorale & Orchestra, and Mozart’s Exsultate, Jubilate with the Sarasota Orchestra. She debuts with Opera Lafayette in the Imposter Unmasked, an immersive pastiche of the English baroque, and with Opera Philadelphia in the world premiere of Luke Styles’ Sitcom, and tours with Thomas Dunford and Ensemble Jupiter in Europe.

She was a member of the 12th edition of Le Jardin des Voix with Les Arts Florissants under William Christie, traveling internationally as La Poésie in Les arts florissants and Proserpine in La Descente d’Orphée aux Enfers by Marc Antoine Charpentier. With Paul Agnew, she debuted with the Monteverdi Festival in Cremona, Italy singing La Fortuna and Damigella in L’incoronazione di Poppea, and has sung in concerts at the Les Arts Florissants spring and summer festivals.

A devoted recitalist, she has presented programs throughout the United States, performing at such venues as the Strathmore Mansion, Washington Performing Arts, Artist Series Concerts of Sarasota, 92NY, Spivey Hall, the Library of Congress, Brevard Music Center, Harvard Musical Association, Woodmere Art Museum, Thomas Jefferson University, and Trust Performing Arts Center. She toured across Latin America and North America with Curtis on Tour and, with Curtis Ensemble 20/21, premiered In the Fields by Tania León. Concert highlights include the Fauré Requiem with the Cleveland Orchestra Youth Orchestra, Poulenc’s Gloria and Dvořák’s Te Deum with the Wichita Symphony Orchestra, Handel’s Messiah with Hudson Baroque, the Brahms Requiem with the Dalton Chorale, and songs with Tempesta di Mare.

Sarah is the recipient of the 2026 Career Advancement Award from the Musical Fund Society and the 2026 Rising Star Award from the Emerging Artists Foundation. She was also named the 2025 winner — and first ever vocalist — to receive the Arthur W. Foote Award from the Harvard Musical Association, a district winner of the 2025 Metropolitan Opera Laffont Competition, the first-place winner of the 2024 MI Opera and 2023 Hal Leonard Vocal Competitions, the emerging artist winner of the 2023 Rochester Oratorio Society Competition, and the winner of the 2022 Shirley Rabb Winston Scholarship by the National Society of Arts and Letters. She has received grants from the George London Foundation, Voce di Meche, and the Gerda Lissner Foundation, and awards from the Opera Awards Foundation, the Opera Index Foundation, the Orpheus Vocal Competition, the Camille Coloratura Awards, and the Mascarade Opera Foundation.

She has trained at the Georg Solti Accademia in Tuscany, the Aspen Music Festival as a Renée Fleming Artist, HGO’s YAVA, the Music Academy of the West, and the Atelier Lyrique at the Verbier Festival. She completed her Master’s of Music and Bachelor’s of Music degrees at the Curtis Institute of Music. Prior to Curtis, she attended Columbia University and the Juilliard Exchange program.
